title: Grateful Dead Live at Oakland Auditorium Arena on 1982-12-28
source: SBD > MC > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Clear soundboard recording with a killer first‑set and a funky, vocal‑flubbed Shakedown Street that shines despite a sleepy second set.
ai_review.review: The SBD capture is crisp and surprisingly clear – even the patched Baby Blue moment sounds solid. The first half of the show delivers several highlights (Jack Straw, Lazy Lightning→Deal, Touch of Grey, Morning Dew) while the second set drifts into a sluggish vibe, though Shakedown Street still erupts into an unforgettable groove despite Jerry’s lyrical slip‑ups.

ai_rating.rationale: Broad consensus of good recording quality and strong first‑set performances balanced by mixed opinions on the second set; many reviewers give 4–5 stars, pulling the overall rating into the high‑four range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Sound is clear and well‑balanced throughout; a patch from another B+ SBD for Baby Blue is noted but does not detract. No major dropouts, just occasional vocal flubs that are musical rather than technical issues.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A strong, song‑rich first set that keeps the energy high, followed by a more languid second set; Shakedown Street serves as the highlight of the latter half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocal flubs on Shakedown and Terrapin are noted, but his guitar solo is praised as brilliant, funky, and a groove‑driver.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass thumps are highlighted during the deep Shakedown groove, providing a funk heartbeat.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby’s rap in Satisfaction and occasional lyric reminders add humor; his fills complement the jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (keyboard) is praised for mirroring Jerry, adding flourishes, and enhancing the Shakedown jam with tasteful fills.
band_member_comments.Drums: Both drummers are lauded for a deep, loose groove that drives the second‑half improvisations.
